rules.title: Salary thresholds
rules.text: The general threshold is £41,700 a year, or the going rate for the job if higher. Lower thresholds apply to new entrants, some PhD holders and jobs on the Immigration Salary List.

rules.title: Changing employer
rules.text: You must make a new application, with a new Certificate of Sponsorship, before you start the new job.

rules.title: Older rules for some workers
rules.text: People first sponsored before 22 July 2025 may continue on older, lower thresholds in some situations. We check which rules apply to you.

rules.title: Settlement
rules.text: Under the government’s plans, Skilled Workers earning £50,271 or more in 3 of the last 5 years keep a 5-year route to ILR. [Read about the ILR changes](/ilr-changes-2026/)

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: Skilled Worker visa requirements
sections.text: You need a job offer from a UK employer with a sponsor licence, a Certificate of Sponsorship, a job at the required skill level (degree level for most new roles since July 2025), a salary of at least £41,700 or the going rate if higher, and English at B2 level. You may also need £1,270 in savings unless your employer certifies your maintenance.

sections.heading: Employers: hiring a Skilled Worker
sections.text: If you want to sponsor workers, you need a [sponsor licence](/sponsor-licence/) first, and you must meet ongoing [compliance duties](/sponsor-licence-compliance/). We help employers with both.

faqs.q: What is the minimum salary for a Skilled Worker visa?
faqs.a: The general threshold is £41,700 a year, or the going rate for the job if higher. Some applicants qualify for lower thresholds.

faqs.q: Can I change jobs on a Skilled Worker visa?
faqs.a: Yes, but you need a new application with a new Certificate of Sponsorship before you start the new job.
